verses.original: וַיֵּ֖דַע יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־ צְרֻיָ֑ה כִּֽי־ לֵ֥ב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־ אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·ḏa‘ yō·w·’āḇ ben- ṣə·ru·yāh kî- lêḇ ham·me·leḵ ‘al- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: Now Joab son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart longed for Absalom
verses.literalPt: CONHECENDO, pois, Joabe, filho de Zeruia, que o coração do rei estava inclinado para Absalão,

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יוֹאָב֙ תְּק֔וֹעָה וַיִּקַּ֥ח מִשָּׁ֖ם אִשָּׁ֣ה חֲכָמָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵ֠לֶיהָ הִֽתְאַבְּלִי־ נָ֞א וְלִבְשִׁי־ נָ֣א בִגְדֵי־ אֵ֗בֶל וְאַל־ תָּס֙וּכִי֙ שֶׁ֔מֶן וְהָיִ֕ית כְּאִשָּׁ֗ה זֶ֚ה יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים מִתְאַבֶּ֖לֶת עַל־ מֵֽת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·laḥ yō·w·’āḇ tə·qō·w·‘āh way·yiq·qaḥ miš·šām ’iš·šāh ḥă·ḵā·māh way·yō·mer ’ê·le·hā hiṯ·’ab·bə·lî- nā wə·liḇ·šî- nā ḇiḡ·ḏê- ’ê·ḇel wə·’al- tā·sū·ḵî še·men wə·hā·yîṯ kə·’iš·šāh zeh yā·mîm rab·bîm miṯ·’ab·be·leṯ ‘al- mêṯ
verses.literal: So Joab sent to Tekoa to bring a wise woman from there He told her . . . Please pretend to be a mourner put on . . . clothes for mourning and do not anoint yourself with oil Act like a woman . . . who has mourned for the dead a long time
verses.literalPt: Enviou Joabe a Tecoa, e tomou de lá uma mulher e disse-lhe: Ora, finge que estás de luto; veste roupas de luto, e não te unjas com óleo, e sê como uma mulher que há já muitos dias está de luto por algum morto.

verses.original: וּבָאת֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְדִבַּ֥רְתְּ אֵלָ֖יו כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיָּ֧שֶׂם יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּפִֽיהָ׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḇāṯ ’el- ham·me·leḵ wə·ḏib·bart ’ê·lāw kad·dā·ḇār haz·zeh way·yā·śem yō·w·’āḇ ’eṯ- had·də·ḇā·rîm bə·p̄î·hā
verses.literal: Then go to the king and speak these words to him And Joab put the words in her mouth
verses.literalPt: E vai ao rei, e fala-lhe conforme a esta palavra. E Joabe lhe pôs as palavras na boca.

verses.original: וַ֠תֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֤ה הַתְּקֹעִית֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתִּפֹּ֧ל עַל־ אַפֶּ֛יהָ אַ֖רְצָה וַתִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר הוֹשִׁ֥עָה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer hā·’iš·šāh hat·tə·qō·‘îṯ ’el- ham·me·leḵ wat·tip·pōl ‘al- ’ap·pe·hā ’ar·ṣāh wat·tiš·tā·ḥū wat·tō·mer hō·wō·ši·‘āh ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: When the woman from Tekoa went to the king she fell facedown . . . in homage and said Help me O king
verses.literalPt: E a mulher tecoíta falou ao rei, e, deitando-se com o rosto em terra, se prostrou e disse: Salva-me, ó rei.

verses.original: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ לָ֥הּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מַה־ לָּ֑ךְ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֲבָ֛ל אִשָּֽׁה־ אַלְמָנָ֥ה אָ֖נִי וַיָּ֥מָת אִישִֽׁי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer- lāh ham·me·leḵ mah- lāḵ wat·tō·mer ’ă·ḇāl ’iš·šāh- ’al·mā·nāh ’ā·nî way·yā·māṯ ’î·šî
verses.literal: What troubles you the king asked her Indeed she said I am a widow for my husband is dead
verses.literalPt: E disse-lhe o rei: Que tens? E disse ela: Na verdade sou mulher viúva; morreu meu marido.

verses.original: וּלְשִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֙ שְׁנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים וַיִּנָּצ֤וּ שְׁנֵיהֶם֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּ֖יל בֵּֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּכּ֧וֹ הָאֶחָ֛ד אֶת־ הָאֶחָ֖ד וַיָּ֥מֶת אֹתֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: ū·lə·šip̄·ḥā·ṯə·ḵā šə·nê ḇā·nîm way·yin·nā·ṣū šə·nê·hem baś·śā·ḏeh wə·’ên maṣ·ṣîl bê·nê·hem way·yak·kōw hā·’e·ḥāḏ ’eṯ- hā·’e·ḥāḏ way·yā·meṯ ’ō·ṯōw
verses.literal: And your maidservant had two sons who were fighting in the field with no one to separate them and one struck the other and killed him
verses.literalPt: Tinha, pois, a tua serva dois filhos, e estes brigaram entre si no campo, e não houve quem os apartasse; assim um feriu ao outro, e o matou.

verses.original: וְהִנֵּה֩ קָ֨מָה כָֽל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֜ה עַל־ שִׁפְחָתֶ֗ךָ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ תְּנִ֣י׀ אֶת־ מַכֵּ֣ה אָחִ֗יו וּנְמִתֵ֙הוּ֙ בְּנֶ֤פֶשׁ אָחִיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָרָ֔ג וְנַשְׁמִ֖ידָה גַּ֣ם אֶת־ הַיּוֹרֵ֑שׁ וְכִבּ֗וּ אֶת־ גַּֽחַלְתִּי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאָ֔רָה לְבִלְתִּ֧י שׂוּם לְאִישִׁ֛י שֵׁ֥ם וּשְׁאֵרִ֖ית עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃פ
verses.transliteration: wə·hin·nêh qā·māh ḵāl ham·miš·pā·ḥāh ‘al- šip̄·ḥā·ṯe·ḵā way·yō·mə·rū tə·nî ’eṯ- mak·kêh ’ā·ḥîw ū·nə·mi·ṯê·hū bə·ne·p̄eš ’ā·ḥîw ’ă·šer hā·rāḡ wə·naš·mî·ḏāh gam ’eṯ- hay·yō·w·rêš wə·ḵib·bū ’eṯ- ga·ḥal·tî ’ă·šer niš·’ā·rāh lə·ḇil·tî śūm lə·’î·šî šêm ū·šə·’ê·rîṯ ‘al- pə·nê hā·’ă·ḏā·māh
verses.literal: Now the whole clan has risen up against your maidservant and said Hand over the one who struck down his brother that we may put him to death for the life of the brother whom he killed Then we will cut off the heir as well So they would extinguish my one remaining ember by not preserving my husband’s name or posterity on . . . the earth
verses.literalPt: E eis que toda a linhagem se levantou contra a tua serva, e disseram: Dá-nos aquele que feriu a seu irmão, para que o matemos, por causa da vida de seu irmão, a quem matou, e para que destruamos também ao herdeiro. Assim apagarão a brasa que me ficou, de sorte que não deixam a meu marido nome, nem remanescente sobre a terra.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ הָאִשָּׁ֖ה לְכִ֣י לְבֵיתֵ֑ךְ וַאֲנִ֖י אֲצַוֶּ֥ה עָלָֽיִךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’el- hā·’iš·šāh lə·ḵî lə·ḇê·ṯêḵ wa·’ă·nî ’ă·ṣaw·weh ‘ā·lā·yiḵ
verses.literal: Go home the king said to the woman and I will give orders on your behalf
verses.literalPt: E disse o rei à mulher: Vai para tua casa; e eu mandarei ordem acerca de ti.

verses.original: וַתֹּ֜אמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֤ה הַתְּקוֹעִית֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עָלַ֞י אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ הֶעָוֺ֖ן וְעַל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ וְכִסְא֖וֹ נָקִֽי׃ס
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer hā·’iš·šāh hat·tə·qō·w·‘îṯ ’el- ham·me·leḵ ‘ā·lay ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ he·‘ā·wōn wə·‘al- bêṯ ’ā·ḇî wə·ham·me·leḵ wə·ḵis·’ōw nā·qî
verses.literal: But the woman of Tekoa said to the king My lord the king may any blame be on me and on my father’s house and may the king and his throne be guiltless
verses.literalPt: E disse a mulher tecoíta ao rei: A injustiça, rei meu SENHOR, venha sobre mim e sobre a casa de meu pai; e o rei e o seu trono fique inculpável.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ הַֽמְדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלַ֙יִךְ֙ וַֽהֲבֵאת֣וֹ אֵלַ֔י וְלֹֽא־ יֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד לָגַ֥עַת בָּֽךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ham·ḏab·bêr ’ê·la·yiḵ wa·hă·ḇê·ṯōw ’ê·lay wə·lō- yō·sîp̄ ‘ō·wḏ lā·ḡa·‘aṯ bāḵ
verses.literal: If anyone speaks to you said the king bring him to me and he will not trouble you again . . .
verses.literalPt: E disse o rei: Quem falar contra ti, traze-mo a mim; e nunca mais te tocará.

verses.original: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ יִזְכָּר־ נָ֨א הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ מֵהַרְבִּית גֹּאֵ֤ל הַדָּם֙ לְשַׁחֵ֔ת וְלֹ֥א יַשְׁמִ֖ידוּ אֶת־ בְּנִ֑י וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ חַי־ יְהוָ֔ה אִם־ יִפֹּ֛ל מִשַּׂעֲרַ֥ת בְּנֵ֖ךְ אָֽרְצָה׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer yiz·kār- nā ham·me·leḵ ’eṯ- Yah·weh ’ĕ·lō·he·ḵā mē·har·bīṯ gō·’êl had·dām lə·ša·ḥêṯ wə·lō yaš·mî·ḏū ’eṯ- bə·nî way·yō·mer ḥay- Yah·weh ’im- yip·pōl miś·śa·‘ă·raṯ bə·nêḵ ’ā·rə·ṣāh
verses.literal: Please she replied may the king invoke the LORD your God to prevent the avenger of blood from increasing the devastation so that my son may not be destroyed As surely as the LORD lives he vowed not a hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground
verses.literalPt: E disse ela: Ora, lembre-se o rei do SENHOR seu Deus, para que os vingadores do sangue não prossigam na destruição, e não exterminem a meu filho. Então disse ele: Vive o SENHOR, que não há de cair no chão nem um dos cabelos de teu filho.

verses.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה תְּדַבֶּר־ נָ֧א שִׁפְחָתְךָ֛ אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָ֑ר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽרִי׃ס
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer hā·’iš·šāh tə·ḏab·ber- nā šip̄·ḥā·ṯə·ḵā ’el- ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ dā·ḇār way·yō·mer dab·bê·rî
verses.literal: Then the woman said Please may your servant speak a word to my lord the king Speak he replied
verses.literalPt: Então disse a mulher: Peço-te que a tua serva fale uma palavra ao rei meu senhor. E disse ele: Fala.

verses.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְלָ֧מָּה חָשַׁ֛בְתָּה כָּזֹ֖את עַל־ עַ֣ם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וּמִדַּבֵּ֨ר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ כְּאָשֵׁ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֛י הָשִׁ֥יב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶֽת־ נִדְּחֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer hā·’iš·šāh wə·lām·māh ḥā·šaḇ·tāh kā·zōṯ ‘al- ‘am ’ĕ·lō·hîm ū·mid·dab·bêr ham·me·leḵ had·dā·ḇār haz·zeh kə·’ā·šêm lə·ḇil·tî hā·šîḇ ham·me·leḵ ’eṯ- nid·də·ḥōw
verses.literal: The woman asked Why have you devised a thing like this against the people of God When the king says this . . . does he not convict himself since he has not brought back his own banished son
verses.literalPt: E disse a mulher: Por que, pois, pensaste tu uma tal coisa contra o povo de Deus? Porque, falando o rei tal palavra, fica como culpado; visto que o rei não torna a trazer o seu desterrado.

verses.original: כִּי־ מ֣וֹת נָמ֔וּת וְכַמַּ֙יִם֙ הַנִּגָּרִ֣ים אַ֔רְצָה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֣א יֵאָסֵ֑פוּ וְלֹֽא־ יִשָּׂ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ נֶ֔פֶשׁ וְחָשַׁב֙ מַֽחֲשָׁב֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּ֛י יִדַּ֥ח מִמֶּ֖נּוּ נִדָּֽח׃
verses.transliteration: kî- mō·wṯ nā·mūṯ wə·ḵam·ma·yim han·nig·gā·rîm ’ar·ṣāh ’ă·šer lō yê·’ā·sê·p̄ū wə·lō- yiś·śā ’ĕ·lō·hîm ne·p̄eš wə·ḥā·šaḇ ma·ḥă·šā·ḇō·wṯ lə·ḇil·tî yid·daḥ mim·men·nū nid·dāḥ
verses.literal: For we will surely die . . . and be like water poured out on the ground which cannot be recovered Yet God does not take away a life but He devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him
verses.literalPt: Porque certamente morreremos, e seremos como águas derramadas na terra que não se ajuntam mais; Deus, pois, lhe não tirará a vida, mas cogita meios, para que não fique banido dele o seu desterrado.

verses.original: וְ֠עַתָּה אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֜אתִי לְדַבֵּ֨ר אֶל־ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲדֹנִי֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֥י יֵֽרְאֻ֖נִי הָעָ֑ם וַתֹּ֤אמֶר שִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֙ אֲדַבְּרָה־ נָּ֣א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אוּלַ֛י יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־ דְּבַ֥ר אֲמָתֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·‘at·tāh ’ă·šer- bā·ṯî lə·ḏab·bêr ’el- ham·me·leḵ ’ă·ḏō·nî ’eṯ- had·dā·ḇār haz·zeh kî yê·rə·’u·nî hā·‘ām wat·tō·mer šip̄·ḥā·ṯə·ḵā ’ă·ḏab·bə·rāh- nā ’el- ham·me·leḵ ’ū·lay ya·‘ă·śeh ham·me·leḵ ’eṯ- də·ḇar ’ă·mā·ṯōw
verses.literal: Now therefore I have come to present this matter to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid Your servant thought I will speak . . . to the king Perhaps he will grant the request of his maidservant
verses.literalPt: E se eu agora vim falar esta palavra ao rei, meu senhor, é porque o povo me atemorizou; dizia, pois, a tua serva: Falarei, pois, ao rei; porventura fará o rei segundo a palavra da sua serva.

verses.original: כִּ֚י יִשְׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־ אֲמָת֖וֹ מִכַּ֣ף הָאִ֑ישׁ לְהַשְׁמִ֨יד אֹתִ֤י וְאֶת־ בְּנִי֙ יַ֔חַד מִֽנַּחֲלַ֖ת אֱלֹהִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: kî yiš·ma‘ ham·me·leḵ lə·haṣ·ṣîl ’eṯ- ’ă·mā·ṯōw mik·kap̄ hā·’îš lə·haš·mîḏ ’ō·ṯî wə·’eṯ- bə·nî ya·ḥaḏ min·na·ḥă·laṯ ’ĕ·lō·hîm
verses.literal: For the king will hear and deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man who would cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance
verses.literalPt: Porque o rei ouvirá, para livrar a sua serva da mão do homem que intenta destruir juntamente a mim e a meu filho da herança de Deus.

verses.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ שִׁפְחָ֣תְךָ֔ יִֽהְיֶה־ נָּ֛א דְּבַר־ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לִמְנוּחָ֑ה כִּ֣י׀ כְּמַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים כֵּ֣ן אֲדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לִשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ הַטּ֣וֹב וְהָרָ֔ע וַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יְהִ֥י עִמָּֽךְ׃פ
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer šip̄·ḥā·ṯə·ḵā yih·yeh- nā də·ḇar- ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ lim·nū·ḥāh kî kə·mal·’aḵ hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm kên ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ liš·mō·a‘ haṭ·ṭō·wḇ wə·hā·rā‘ Yah·weh ’ĕ·lō·he·ḵā yə·hî ‘im·māḵ
verses.literal: And now your servant . . . says May the word of my lord the king bring me rest for my lord the king is able to discern good and evil just like the angel of God . . . May the LORD your God be with you
verses.literalPt: Dizia mais a tua serva: Seja agora a palavra do rei meu senhor para descanso; porque como um anjo de Deus, assim é o rei, meu SENHOR, para ouvir o bem e o mal; e o SENHOR teu Deus será contigo.

verses.original: וַיַּ֣עַן הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַל־ נָ֨א תְכַחֲדִ֤י מִמֶּ֙נִּי֙ דָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י שֹׁאֵ֣ל אֹתָ֑ךְ וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה יְדַבֶּר־ נָ֖א אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘an ham·me·leḵ way·yō·mer ’el- hā·’iš·šāh ’al- nā ṯə·ḵa·ḥă·ḏî mim·men·nî dā·ḇār ’ă·šer ’ā·nō·ḵî šō·’êl ’ō·ṯāḵ wat·tō·mer hā·’iš·šāh yə·ḏab·ber- nā ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: Then the king said to the woman I am going to ask you something do not . . . conceal it from me Let my lord the king speak . . . she replied
verses.literalPt: Então respondeu o rei, e disse à mulher: Peço-te que não me encubras o que eu te perguntar. E disse a mulher: Ora fale o rei, meu senhor.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הֲיַ֥ד יוֹאָ֛ב אִתָּ֖ךְ בְּכָל־ זֹ֑את וַתַּ֣עַן הָאִשָּׁ֣ה וַתֹּ֡אמֶר חֵֽי־ נַפְשְׁךָ֩ אֲדֹנִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אִם־ אִ֣שׁ׀ לְהֵמִ֣ין וּלְהַשְׂמִ֗יל מִכֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי־ עַבְדְּךָ֤ יוֹאָב֙ ה֣וּא צִוָּ֔נִי וְה֗וּא שָׂ֚ם בְּפִ֣י שִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֔ אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ hă·yaḏ yō·w·’āḇ ’it·tāḵ bə·ḵāl zōṯ wat·ta·‘an hā·’iš·šāh wat·tō·mer ḥê- nap̄·šə·ḵā ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ ’im- ’iš lə·hê·mîn ū·lə·haś·mîl mik·kōl ’ă·šer- dib·ber ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ kî- ‘aḇ·də·ḵā yō·w·’āḇ hū ṣiw·wā·nî wə·hū śām bə·p̄î šip̄·ḥā·ṯə·ḵā ’êṯ kāl- had·də·ḇā·rîm hā·’êl·leh
verses.literal: So the king asked Is the hand of Joab behind all this The woman . . . answered As surely as you live my lord the king no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything that my lord the king says Yes your servant Joab is the one who gave me orders he told . . . your maidservant - exactly what to say . . .
verses.literalPt: E disse o rei: Não é verdade que a mão de Joabe anda contigo em tudo isto? E respondeu a mulher, e disse: Vive a tua alma, ó rei meu senhor, que ninguém se poderá desviar, nem para a direita nem para a esquerda, de tudo quanto o rei, meu senhor, tem falado: Porque Joabe, teu servo, é quem me deu ordem, e foi ele que pôs na boca da tua serva todas estas palavras:

verses.original: לְבַעֲב֤וּר סַבֵּב֙ אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י הַדָּבָ֔ר עָשָׂ֛ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ יוֹאָ֖ב אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַאדֹנִ֣י חָכָ֗ם כְּחָכְמַת֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לָדַ֖עַת אֶֽת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃ס
verses.transliteration: lə·ḇa·‘ă·ḇūr sab·bêḇ ’eṯ- pə·nê had·dā·ḇār ‘ā·śāh ‘aḇ·də·ḵā yō·w·’āḇ ’eṯ- had·dā·ḇār haz·zeh wa·ḏō·nî ḥā·ḵām kə·ḥā·ḵə·maṯ mal·’aḵ hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm lā·ḏa·‘aṯ ’eṯ- kāl- ’ă·šer bā·’ā·reṣ
verses.literal: Joab - your servant has done this to bring about this change of affairs but my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God to know everything that happens in the land
verses.literalPt: Para mudar o aspecto deste caso foi que o teu servo Joabe fez isto; porém sábio é meu senhor, conforme à sabedoria de um anjo de Deus, para entender tudo o que há na terra.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב הִנֵּה־ נָ֥א עָשִׂ֖יתִי אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְלֵ֛ךְ הָשֵׁ֥ב אֶת־ הַנַּ֖עַר אֶת־ אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’el- yō·w·’āḇ hin·nêh- nā ‘ā·śî·ṯî ’eṯ- had·dā·ḇār haz·zeh wə·lêḵ hā·šêḇ ’eṯ- han·na·‘ar ’eṯ- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: Then the king said to Joab . . . . . . I hereby grant this request Go bring back the young man Absalom
verses.literalPt: Então o rei disse a Joabe: Eis que fiz isto; vai, pois, e torna a trazer o jovem Absalão.

verses.original: וַיִּפֹּל֩ יוֹאָ֨ב אֶל־ פָּנָ֥יו אַ֛רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡ב הַיּוֹם֩ יָדַ֨ע עַבְדְּךָ֜ כִּי־ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־ דְּבַ֥ר עַבְדּוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yip·pōl yō·w·’āḇ ’el- pā·nāw ’ar·ṣāh way·yiš·ta·ḥū way·ḇā·reḵ ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ way·yō·mer yō·w·’āḇ hay·yō·wm yā·ḏa‘ ‘aḇ·də·ḵā kî- mā·ṣā·ṯî ḥên bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ ’ă·šer- ‘ā·śāh ham·me·leḵ ’eṯ- də·ḇar ʿaḇ·dō
verses.literal: Joab fell facedown . . . in homage and blessed the king Today said Joab your servant knows that he has found favor in your eyes my lord the king because the king has granted his request
verses.literalPt: Então Joabe se prostrou sobre o seu rosto em terra, e se inclinou, e agradeceu ao rei; e disse Joabe: Hoje conhece o teu servo que achei graça aos teus olhos, ó rei meu senhor, porque o rei fez segundo a palavra do teu servo.

verses.original: וַיָּ֥קָם יוֹאָ֖ב וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ גְּשׁ֑וּרָה וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת־ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yā·qām yō·w·’āḇ way·yê·leḵ gə·šū·rāh way·yā·ḇê ’eṯ- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm yə·rū·šā·lim
verses.literal: So Joab got up went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem
verses.literalPt: Levantou-se, pois, Joabe, e foi a Gesur, e trouxe Absalão a Jerusalém.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ יִסֹּ֣ב אֶל־ בֵּית֔וֹ וּפָנַ֖י לֹ֣א יִרְאֶ֑ה וַיִּסֹּ֤ב אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־ בֵּית֔וֹ וּפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א רָאָֽה׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ yis·sōḇ ’el- bê·ṯōw ū·p̄ā·nay lō yir·’eh way·yis·sōḇ ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’el- bê·ṯōw ū·p̄ə·nê ham·me·leḵ lō rā·’āh
verses.literal: But the king added He may return to his house but he must not see my face So Absalom returned to his own house but he did not see the face of the king
verses.literalPt: E disse o rei: Torne para a sua casa, e não veja a minha face. Tornou, pois, Absalão para sua casa, e não viu a face do rei.

verses.original: וּכְאַבְשָׁל֗וֹם לֹא־ הָיָ֧ה אִישׁ־ יָפֶ֛ה בְּכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַלֵּ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד מִכַּ֤ף רַגְלוֹ֙ וְעַ֣ד קָדְקֳד֔וֹ לֹא־ הָ֥יָה ב֖וֹ מֽוּם׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḵə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm lō- hā·yāh ’îš- yā·p̄eh bə·ḵāl yiś·rā·’êl lə·hal·lêl mə·’ōḏ mik·kap̄ raḡ·lōw wə·‘aḏ qā·ḏə·qo·ḏōw lō- hā·yāh ḇōw mūm
verses.literal: Now there was not a man in all Israel as handsome and highly praised as Absalom From the sole of his foot to the top of his head he did not have a single flaw
verses.literalPt: Não havia, porém, em todo o Israel homem tão belo e tão aprazível como Absalão; desde a planta do pé até à cabeça não havia nele defeito algum.

verses.original: וּֽבְגַלְּחוֹ֮ אֶת־ רֹאשׁוֹ֒ וְֽ֠הָיָה מִקֵּ֨ץ יָמִ֤ים׀ לַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְגַלֵּ֔חַ כִּֽי־ כָבֵ֥ד עָלָ֖יו וְגִלְּח֑וֹ וְשָׁקַל֙ אֶת־ שְׂעַ֣ר רֹאשׁ֔וֹ מָאתַ֥יִם שְׁקָלִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥בֶן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḇə·ḡal·lə·ḥōw ’eṯ- rō·šōw wə·hā·yāh miq·qêṣ yā·mîm lay·yā·mîm ’ă·šer yə·ḡal·lê·aḥ kî- ḵā·ḇêḏ ‘ā·lāw wə·ḡil·lə·ḥōw wə·šā·qal ’eṯ- śə·‘ar rō·šōw mā·ṯa·yim šə·qā·lîm bə·’e·ḇen ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: And when he cut the hair of his head . . . he shaved it every year . . . . . . because his hair got so heavy . . . . . . he would weigh it out . . . to be two hundred shekels according to the royal standard
verses.literalPt: E, quando tosquiava a sua cabeça (e sucedia que no fim de cada ano a tosquiava, porquanto muito lhe pesava, e por isso a tosquiava), pesava o cabelo da sua cabeça duzentos siclos, segundo o peso real.

verses.original: וַיִּֽוָּלְד֤וּ לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ שְׁלוֹשָׁ֣ה בָנִ֔ים וּבַ֥ת אַחַ֖ת וּשְׁמָ֣הּ תָּמָ֑ר הִ֣יא הָיְתָ֔ה אִשָּׁ֖ה יְפַ֥ת מַרְאֶֽה׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yiw·wā·lə·ḏū lə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm šə·lō·wō·šāh ḇā·nîm ū·ḇaṯ ’a·ḥaṯ ū·šə·māh tā·mār hî hā·yə·ṯāh ’iš·šāh yə·p̄aṯ mar·’eh
verses.literal: Three sons were born to Absalom and a daughter named Tamar who was a beautiful . . . woman
verses.literalPt: Também nasceram a Absalão três filhos e uma filha, cujo nome era Tamar; e esta era mulher formosa à vista.

verses.original: וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב אַבְשָׁל֛וֹם בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֑ים וּפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א רָאָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·šeḇ ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm bî·rū·šā·lim šə·nā·ṯa·yim yā·mîm ū·p̄ə·nê ham·me·leḵ lō rā·’āh
verses.literal: Now Absalom lived in Jerusalem two years without seeing the face of the king
verses.literalPt: Assim ficou Absalão dois anos inteiros em Jerusalém, e não viu a face do rei.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אַבְשָׁל֜וֹם אֶל־ יוֹאָ֗ב לִשְׁלֹ֤חַ אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לָב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח עוֹד֙ שֵׁנִ֔ית וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לָבֽוֹא׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·laḥ ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’el- yō·w·’āḇ liš·lō·aḥ ’ō·ṯōw ’el- ham·me·leḵ wə·lō ’ā·ḇāh lā·ḇō·w ’ê·lāw way·yiš·laḥ ‘ō·wḏ šê·nîṯ wə·lō ’ā·ḇāh lā·ḇō·w
verses.literal: Then he sent for Joab to send him to the king but Joab refused . . . to come to him So Absalom sent a second time but Joab still would not . . . come
verses.literalPt: Mandou, pois, Absalão chamar a Joabe, para o enviar ao rei; porém não quis vir a ele; e enviou ainda segunda vez e, contudo, não quis vir.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֶל־ עֲבָדָ֜יו רְאוּ֩ חֶלְקַ֨ת יוֹאָ֤ב אֶל־ יָדִי֙ וְלוֹ־ שָׁ֣ם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים לְכ֖וּ וְהוֹצִתִּיהָ בָאֵ֑שׁ וַיַּצִּ֜תוּ עַבְדֵ֧י אַבְשָׁל֛וֹם אֶת־ הַחֶלְקָ֖ה בָּאֵֽשׁ׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’el- ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw rə·’ū ḥel·qaṯ yō·w·’āḇ ’el- yā·ḏî wə·lōw- šām śə·‘ō·rîm lə·ḵū wə·hō·ṣit·tī·hå̄ ḇā·’êš way·yaṣ·ṣi·ṯū ‘aḇ·ḏê ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’eṯ- ha·ḥel·qāh bā·’êš
verses.literal: Then Absalom said to his servants Look Joab’s field is next to mine and he has barley there Go and set it on fire And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire . . .
verses.literalPt: Então disse aos seus servos: Vedes ali o pedaço de campo de Joabe pegado ao meu, e tem cevada nele; ide, e ponde-lhe fogo. E os servos de Absalão puseram fogo ao pedaço de campo.

verses.original: וַיָּ֣קָם יוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם הַבָּ֑יְתָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו לָ֣מָּה הִצִּ֧יתוּ עֲבָדֶ֛ךָ אֶת־ הַחֶלְקָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־ לִ֖י בָּאֵֽשׁ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·qām yō·w·’āḇ way·yā·ḇō ’el- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm hab·bā·yə·ṯāh way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw lām·māh hiṣ·ṣî·ṯū ‘ă·ḇā·ḏe·ḵā ’eṯ- ha·ḥel·qāh ’ă·šer- lî bā·’êš
verses.literal: Then Joab came to Absalom’s house and demanded . . . Why did your servants set my field on fire
verses.literalPt: Então Joabe se levantou, e veio a Absalão, em casa, e disse-lhe: Por que puseram os teus servos fogo ao pedaço de campo que é meu?

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם אֶל־ יוֹאָ֡ב הִנֵּ֣ה שָׁלַ֣חְתִּי אֵלֶ֣יךָ׀ לֵאמֹ֡ר בֹּ֣א הֵ֠נָּה וְאֶשְׁלְחָה֩ אֹתְךָ֨ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֗ר לָ֤מָּה בָּ֙אתִי֙ מִגְּשׁ֔וּר ט֥וֹב לִ֖י עֹ֣ד אֲנִי־ שָׁ֑ם וְעַתָּ֗ה אֶרְאֶה֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאִם־ יֶשׁ־ בִּ֥י עָוֺ֖ן וֶהֱמִתָֽנִי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’el- yō·w·’āḇ hin·nêh šā·laḥ·tî ’ê·le·ḵā lê·mōr bō hên·nāh wə·’eš·lə·ḥāh ’ō·ṯə·ḵā ’el- ham·me·leḵ lê·mōr lām·māh bā·ṯî mig·gə·šūr ṭō·wḇ lî ‘ōḏ ’ă·nî- šām wə·‘at·tāh ’er·’eh pə·nê ham·me·leḵ wə·’im- yeš- bî ‘ā·wōn we·hĕ·mi·ṯā·nî
verses.literal: Look said Absalom - I sent for you and said Come here I want to send you to the king to ask Why have I come back from Geshur It would be better for me if I were still there So now let me see the king’s face and if there is iniquity in me let him kill me
verses.literalPt: E disse Absalão a Joabe: Eis que enviei a ti, dizendo: Vem cá, para que te envie ao rei, a dizer-lhe: Para que vim de Gesur? Melhor me fora estar ainda lá. Agora, pois, veja eu a face do rei; e, se há ainda em mim alguma culpa, que me mate.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א יוֹאָ֣ב אֶל־ הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ וַיַּגֶּד־ לוֹ֒ וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֨חוּ ל֧וֹ עַל־ אַפָּ֛יו אַ֖רְצָה לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשַּׁ֥ק הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְאַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃פ

verses.literal: So Joab went - and told the king and David summoned Absalom who came . . . to him and bowed facedown . . . before him . . . Then the king kissed Absalom
verses.literalPt: Então foi Joabe ao rei, e assim lho disse. Então chamou a Absalão, e ele se apresentou ao rei, e se inclinou sobre o seu rosto em terra diante do rei; e o rei beijou a Absalão.
